extracted.intended_audience: PR writers, communications professionals, and web/content writers producing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing scannable, web-optimized press releases that load quickly, use hypertext and multimedia appropriately, and follow accessibility and metadata best practices. Emphasizes concise length, paragraph structure, scannability, and technical elements (schema, Open Graph, responsive images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short
rubrics_metrics.description: Web text should be short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep prose concise for digital readers; 'less is more'—web content typically should be about 50% of equivalent hardcopy text. For press releases, 400–500 words is ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scannable
rubrics_metrics.description: Web text should be scannable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content so users can pick keywords, sentences, and paragraphs of interest rather than reading every word. Use formatting and structure (headings, bullets, bold) to support scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured as linked, topical pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize content as linked pages grouped by topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure press-release content as part of a topical web of pages (related releases, background, bios) rather than a long monolithic document to improve discoverability and navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended length: Web: 50% of hardcopy; Press release: 400–500 words ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for shorter copy online. For press releases specifically, keep total word count under 500 words where possible to match reader expectations and attention spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long continuous blocks of text
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present long continuous paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break up long blocks; long uninterrupted text hinders scanning and increases cognitive load. Prefer multiple short paragraphs each focused on a single idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings / subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use headings and subheadings to structure content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear section headings/subheadings to create scannable sections and allow readers to jump to areas of interest; headings are listed as required for web press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulleted lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bullet points where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present lists, key facts, or features as bullets to improve skim-ability and highlight important details; bulleted lists are a required element for web press releases when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bolding to emphasize keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold a few important terms (not entire sentences) to draw attention during scanning; listed as a recommended/required scannability technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: White space matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use white space to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide margins, line spacing, and paragraph breaks so the page doesn't appear dense; white space aids scanning and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive hyperlinks (hypertext)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use descriptive hyperlinks (not generic 'click here').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to source documents, related releases, research papers (DOI), images/multimedia, and bio pages using descriptive link text so users know destination and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph length (2–4 sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs should be 2–4 sentences; 2–3 sentences ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep paragraphs short, front-load topic sentences, and limit each paragraph to a single idea to support scanning and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single idea per paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paragraph should contain one idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating multiple concepts in a paragraph; single-idea paragraphs help readers extract information quickly during a skim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-load with topic sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Front-load paragraphs with a topic sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the main point at the beginning of the paragraph to align with how users scan and to support inverted-pyramid style for press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alt text on images
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alt text for all images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add descriptive alternative text to images to support accessibility (Section 508/WCAG) and users with assistive technologies; listed as required for web press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-responsive layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the page layout is mobile-responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design press release pages to render correctly on mobile devices (responsive CSS, adaptable images, readable font sizes); mobile responsiveness is a required element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compressed images (fast load)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compress images for fast loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize images to minimize file size while preserving quality; this helps meet page-load performance goals and improves user experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-friendly media formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Use web-friendly formats (JPG, WebP, MP4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select image/video formats optimized for web delivery and compatibility; prefer modern compressed formats (WebP for images, MP4 for video) when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lazy loading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lazy loading for media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer loading below-the-fold images and media until needed to improve initial page-load times and perceived performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive images (multiple sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide responsive images in multiple sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve appropriately sized images for different viewport sizes (srcset, sizes) to reduce bandwidth and speed up rendering on various devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include captions for images/media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise captions to explain visuals and provide context; captions support comprehension and are useful for scanning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded video
rubrics_metrics.description: Include embedded video to increase engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video for demonstrations or key messages, ensuring it is optimized for web (format, bitrate) and includes captions/transcripts for accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interactive data elements to engage readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed charts, interactive visualizations, or data tools to let users explore information; ensure accessibility and performance considerations are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social share buttons / widgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide social sharing widgets/buttons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include social share buttons (listed in implicit rubric) and ensure they are implemented in a way that doesn't significantly harm page load times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related stories / links
rubrics_metrics.description: Link to related stories and related content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to related releases and background content to keep readers in the topical area and provide context; part of hypertext and engagement strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter signup
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a newsletter signup to capture engaged readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a clear and unobtrusive newsletter sign-up element to convert interested readers into subscribers; position it where engagement likelihood is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page loads under 3 seconds
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for page load time under 3 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance target to retain readers and reduce bounce; optimize images, defer noncritical JavaScript, and use caching/CDNs to meet this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schema markup present
rubrics_metrics.description: Include schema markup on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add structured data (e.g., NewsArticle/PressRelease schema) to help search engines and social platforms understand the content and improve discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Graph tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Open Graph metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image, etc.) so social platforms display rich previews when the release is shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitter Card tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Twitter Card metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add Twitter Card tags to control how the press release appears when shared on Twitter (summary, summary_large_image, player card for video).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible (Section 508 / WCAG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the page meets accessibility standards (Section 508 / WCAG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for keyboard navigation, provide alt text, captions/transcripts for media, sufficient color contrast, and semantic HTML to support users with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-aloud test
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate clarity by reading the text aloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy reads clearly and naturally aloud, it likely has appropriate sentence structure and clarity; use this as a quick usability check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skim test
rubrics_metrics.description: Can users extract main points by scanning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a skim test: ensure headings, bullets, and bolded terms let users pick up main messages without reading every word.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-pattern reading optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize layout for F-pattern scanning behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most important elements in the top-left area and use short lines, headings, and emphasized terms consistent with the F-pattern eye movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid (most important first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the inverted-pyramid structure: lead with most important information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load key facts in the opening paragraph so skimmers get the most critical information immediately; follow with supporting details.
